reason: Verified in source and by driving at 1440. The two buttons: render-b.js:681 builds `act("Send the link", true)` and `act("Copy the link")` with no data-act and no attrs, states.publish never calls wireOwner (only ownerSurface does, line 577), and the only delegated click listener lives inside wireOwner. Driven, publish contains exactly two buttons, both `data-act=none`; clicking Send the link and then Copy the link leaves body innerHTML length and innerText byte-identical, and publish renders zero [role=status] nodes, so nothing is announced either. This is the lab's own rule broken on the one screen it matters most: the comment above `inert()` at render-b.js:255 reads "Anything not built is inert text, never a focusable promise", and `.b-inert` exists in b.css:388 and is used in owner-empty. It is also the lesson at lessons.md:16-18 ("Advertising is a promise; the panel checks promises"). And the gate genuinely cannot see it: the dead-control loop at interaction-check.mjs:539 runs over ['owner-flight','owner-empty'] only, so publish is the exact state it never visits. The no-way-back half survives the round-1 'this is a deck, not a prototype' argument because round-1 killed that argument itself: its accepted remediation of owner-verbs-are-advertised-not-built wired Preview and Publish to navigate (render-b.js:520-521 set data-state and remount). The deck now navigates, in one direction only. Driven from owner-flight, Preview lands on desk with 0 buttons, 0 links and 0 focusable elements in the whole document, and because the remount does not touch the URL or push a history entry, the query string still says state=owner-flight and browser Back leaves the lab rather than returning to the plan; Publish is the same trip with two dead controls at the end of it. An owner who presses either is stranded until they reload. Two inaccuracies that do not save it: card() is a real <a href=F.shareUrlFull> so the share URL is technically reachable by right-click-copy-link on the card, and the URL span already computes user-select:auto so it can be dragged and copied by hand. Neither is an affordance a couple would find. No constraint is touched: no fourth colour, no third weight, no family, no reopening of the direction.
sharpenedFix: Right defect; three corrections to the surgery. (1) Do NOT put a share sheet behind Send the link: navigator.share does not exist in desktop Chromium and publish is a `full` medium (MEDIUM map, render-b.js:779), so it would be a second dead button wearing a handler. Make the screen carry one true action: give Copy the link `data-act="copy"` writing F.shareUrlFull (the full URL, not the display-trimmed F.shareUrl) via navigator.clipboard.writeText, flip the label to "Copied" for 2s and restore it, and promote it to `data-primary`. Demote Send the link to `inert(...)` this round per the lab's own rule and round-1's accepted ruling on unbuilt verbs. (2) Publish has no reversibility bar and no live region, so the fix cannot reuse 'the existing role=status bar' - render a polite live region inside states.publish (an empty [role=status] beside .b-note) and write 'Link copied.' into it on success; also handle the clipboard rejection path with 'Copy did not work. Select the link and copy it by hand.' rather than a silent failure. (3) Do NOT add a Back to the plan button inside desk's .b-field. Desk is the audience artifact and round-1's confirmed audience-is-handed-the-owners-dashboard finding exists to keep owner chrome out of it; interaction-check.mjs asserts against desk on that basis, so an in-field owner button trades one confirmed defect for another. Instead return through a preview-only owner strip rendered OUTSIDE the audience field and only when desk was reached by pressing Preview - set a transient flag in the preview branch of the wireOwner handler (render-b.js:520) and have states.desk read it - carrying one action, 'Back to the plan' (data-act="owner"), that sets data-state to owner-flight and remounts. Loading ?state=desk directly must stay byte-identical to today so the frames, shots and desk assertions do not move. Publish IS an owner surface, so there the return belongs in the normal chrome: give states.publish a bar() with a single 'Back to the plan' action. Both require states.publish and the preview-flagged desk to call wireOwner (or a minimal wire) - today neither is wired at all - and the handler needs an `owner` branch beside preview/publish. (4) Widen the gate rather than hand-listing four more states: run the dead-control loop at interaction-check.mjs:539 over every entry in config.states, so no state can ever be born with a focusable promise again, and add one assertion that pressing Copy the link changes the label and writes the [role=status] line.
